utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Would the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the contempt case of Milan Tupajic, case number IT-95-5/18-R77.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I am Presiding Judge O-Gon Kwon in Trial Chamber III. I have been designated to hear this Initial Appearance of Mr. Tupajic. Before we proceed further, I would like to apologies to everyone for the delay which was caused by the technical difficulties which were not fixed yet, so we will do without the LiveNote unless parties are opposed to it. First I would like the counsel appearing for Mr. Tupajic to now introduce himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Eugene O'Sullivan for Mr. Tupajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. O'Sullivan. Although the Chamber decided to prosecute this matter itself pursuant to Rule 77(D)(2), the Prosecution has also been given the option to attend this hearing if it so wishes. I see that Prosecution is also present here today. Could I have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Alan Tieger appearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tupajic, I would now like to ask you whether you are able to follow the proceedings in a language that you understand. Are you receiving the interpretation into your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Kwon, I am receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I first have to go through certain formalities. I'd first like to ask you to state your full name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Milan Tupajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tupajic. And your date and place of your birth for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on the 2nd of June, 1954, at Knezina municipality of Sokolac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Tupajic. You were transferred to the United Nations Detention Unit in The Hague yesterday, i.e., 15th of December, 2011, and can I take it that your family is aware of that transfer?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Upon my arrival to the Detention Unit, I briefly contacted my wife so that she is aware of my whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to check as well that you have received a copy of the Order in Lieu of indictment dated 30th of November, 2011, in your own language and that you have understood its content.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I received it, and I fully understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now you are represented here today by Mr. Eugene O'Sullivan. Are you satisfied with your representation here today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I had the chance to speak to Mr. O'Sullivan twice and for the time being I'm satisfied. How things will develop, I don't know, but I expect the situation to remain unchanged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tupajic, you are being charged with one count of contempt for refusing to comply with the Chamber's first subpoena ad testificandum issued on 23rd September 2011, and the second subpoena ad testificandum issued on 3rd of November, 2011. After you failed to comply with the first subpoena, the Chamber, having found that your reasons put forth in your response did not constitute a just excuse justifying your noncompliance with the subpoena issued a second subpoena, but you continued to refuse to comply. So can I now ask that it is still your position today, Mr. Tupajic? If necessary, we may go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think my reply requires private session. I maintain that the reasons that I stated before the subpoena was served, and I stated them to the OTP in writing, and I also gave them to Mr. Tieger orally, and as well as other reasons that I did not put in writing are justified and constitute a valid foundation for my decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we continue with this initial, Mr. O'Sullivan. Now, Mr. O'Sullivan, the accused is entitled to have the indictment read out in court. Does Mr. Tupajic wish the Order in Lieu of Indictment to be read out now or does he waive that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will defer to Mr. Tupajic on this -- on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tupajic, you are entitled to have the indictment read out in this courtroom now. Would you like that Order in Lieu of Indictment to be read out now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood the order fully, and as for me personally, there is no need for it to be read out. If it is, however, required for the public, I do not oppose that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't think it's necessary. Now pursuant to Rule 62(A)(iii), Mr. Tupajic, you can enter a plea to the charges of contempt set out in the Order in Lieu of Indictment today if you so choose, or you can decide to postpone your plea for a period of up to ten days in accordance with Rule 77(E). Did you discuss this with your counsel, and how do you wish to proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've spoken to counsel about this. We spoke today. But I took my decision earlier, in 2009, and informed the OTP in writing. I believe that a copy of this letter of mine to the OTP should be available. Since June 2009, I have not changed my decision and couldn't change it either, and I stand by it still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think you understood my question. I was asking whether you would like to plead today or postpone it up to ten days. Are you prepared to plead to the charges?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to state my plea today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tupajic, if you could rise, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tupajic, you are charged with contempt of court under Rule 77(A)(iii) of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure I heard the interpretation. Could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead innocent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. I would ask the Registrar to record your plea of not guilty. Mr. Tupajic, in light of the nature of the charge against you and all the circumstances, it is in your interest to have this matter resolved as quickly as possible. Given your plea, this means setting a date for the trial which should be a short hearing of no more than a day or two following which the Chamber will issue its judgement. At that trial you will be entitled to call witnesses, and you may choose to testify yourself. This is all for you to discuss with your counsel. Therefore, I would like to ask you through your counsel how long you consider you will need to prepare for the trial. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I request that we move into private session very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Could the Chamber move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As this is a contempt case and I do not believe that there are any issues of disclosure or that these proceedings should be prolonged unnecessarily, should you wish to file any preliminary motions, you should do so within ten days from today in accordance with Rule 77(E). Do you understand that, Mr. Tupajic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. However, I need assistance by -- by an attorney, because I'm not a lawyer, although I did learn much through my participation in proceedings here. But I cannot afford to hire a lawyer of my own choice whom I would be able to pay, so I ask the Tribunal to appoint a Defence counsel for me so that we can embark on that new process together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I believe that Registry would pay utmost care in appointing a Defence counsel for you. Mr. Tupajic or Mr. O'Sullivan, are there any other matters to be raised today?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: The -- the only other matter, Your Honour, is -- it seemed to be suggested that a trial date will be fixed, and I -- it appears that this will not take place before the end of the winter recess, and therefore I would be requesting that Mr. Tupajic be released and allowed to return home pending the -- the trial in this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would prefer to have it in writing. Could you do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder if you can put it in writing in a motion for provisional release.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With all the formalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tupajic, do you have anything to raise with the Chamber before we adjourn the proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't really have any matters to raise. I'm sorry that I didn't have the opportunity to acquaint this Trial Chamber with all relevant facts. I don't want you to get the impression that I'm doing all I can to -- to not to appear here before this court. That's all that I have, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then -- Mr. Tieger, do you have any observation?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. As the Court noted, I was here on the off chance that some contextual or background information might be helpful, but I don't have anything to add at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. That said, considering the court schedule of the Tribunal, the Chamber will issue a Scheduling Order for the trial in due course and will consider the motion if filed by Mr. O'Sullivan. The hearing is now adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.39 p.m.
